# Fate UI v0.8.2-beta1

This beta fixes clipboard and text editing on macOS and makes the built-in Browser workspace the home for links that appear in the conversation.

## Cross-platform copy, paste, and editing

- Restores copy, paste, cut, select all, undo, and redo keyboard shortcuts on macOS. Fate UI's application menu was missing the Edit submenu, and on macOS Electron only routes Cmd+C / Cmd+V / Cmd+X / Cmd+A / Cmd+Z to the focused field once those menu roles exist. Windows and Linux route the same shortcuts natively and were unaffected, which is why the gap only surfaced for Mac users.
- Adds a consistent right-click edit menu (Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All) for editable fields and selected text across Windows, macOS, and Linux. Each item enables or disables based on what the current selection and field allow.
- Keeps the new menu from duplicating anything. Monaco's editor and the embedded browser already render their own context menus, so the right-click edit menu only appears over plain text fields and selected text in the app's own UI.
- Lets the manual terminal copy its selection. Ctrl+Shift+C on Windows and Linux, and Cmd+C on macOS, now write the terminal selection to the clipboard.

## Open links in the Browser workspace

- Agent mentions, markdown links, and other web links in the conversation now open inside the built-in Browser workspace instead of always handing off to the system browser. Left-click opens in the workspace, middle-click opens another workspace tab, and right-click offers Open in Browser workspace, Open in external browser, or Copy link.
- Validates every link before it reaches the browser. Only credential-free HTTP and HTTPS URLs are accepted, including bare localhost addresses, so crafted or unsafe schemes are ignored.
- Centralizes the open flow so navigation shows the right pending state and surfaces honest toasts when the browser is unavailable or the selected project is not trusted.

## Composer and session reliability

- Stops the model and reasoning-level pills from snapping back when a message is queued. A queued message is still the next user turn, so a staged model or thinking-level change now stays visible in the composer until that turn actually runs or is cancelled.
- Cancelling a queued message releases the captured setting back to the session defaults, but only when nothing newer has been staged in the meantime.

## Workspace

- Raises the Browser workspace's maximum width so it can grow toward a comfortable widescreen viewport on large displays, and centralizes the pane limits into shared constants.

## Compatibility and installers

Existing projects, Pi sessions, settings, themes, Agent Team data, and Git workflows do not require a manual migration. This beta does not add scheduled or background automations, arbitrary desktop control, or an intentional breaking change.

GitHub Actions builds and tests the release natively on Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon, macOS Intel, and Linux x64. The prerelease contains seven installers plus `SHA256SUMS`:

- Windows x64: NSIS `.exe`
- macOS arm64 and x64: `.dmg` and `.pkg`
- Linux x64: `.AppImage` and `.deb`

Public beta installers remain unsigned. Windows SmartScreen or macOS Gatekeeper may show an unknown-publisher warning, so verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS`.
